lines.en: I hop forward, bound after bound.
My bold stripes sway with me.
I push off with my hind legs.
Ears twitch, then I spring.
I slip low through the grass.
One hop carries me far.
I land on leaves, very softly.
A short tuft of a tail.
I hop while watching both sides.
I circle the shrub.
This grass is too short to hide me.
I run a few steps, then freeze.
Both ears lie flat on my back.
I take another path.
I leap over a dry branch.
A hasty hop, but a clean landing.
I crouch, ears standing tall.
I am listening far away.
I flick one ear.
My nose never stops moving.
I tuck myself round.
I lift a forepaw and lick it.
I stare at that shrub.
My stripes stand out in the sun.
I hold still as a stone.
The wind stirs the fur by my ears.
I nibble two bites of grass.
I shift to a different crouch.
The soil is loose; good for digging.
I glance sideways.
My eyes are big; I see well.
Stay still; wait.
I look up, ears twitching.
Your footsteps are too heavy.
I shrink back a little.
Do you have anything to eat?
I turn my head sideways to study you.
Crouch, and I will come closer.
My nose twitches twice.
You're blocking my burrow.
I blink my big eyes.
We keep a certain distance.
I rise, then crouch again.
Stay still and I will dare come near.
I squeal once.
I bolt a long way in one bound.
Something cut my back.
I am shaking badly.
That was too heavy.
My ears are flat to my back.
I run two hops and stop.
The burrow; I need the burrow.
It hurts too much to move.
Please stop chasing me.
I smell carrot.
I close two hops at once.
Give it; do not hold it so high.
My nose is twitching fast.
That is my favourite.
I sit up straight and wait.
One hop around you, stripes flashing.
A little closer.
Not enough to fill a tooth.
Do you have any more on you?
My forepaws are together.
I follow you a while.
Smells sweet.
Let me take one small bite.
If you walk, I will hop along.
Better than the leaves you had.
You touched me; I sprang away.
I jumped and hit you.
I slid a little on landing.
Your step shakes the ground.
I dart past your feet.
I am small; do not step on me.
The bump sends me off course.
I shake myself.
Excuse me; let me through.
I am behind you; do not turn fast.
I lay my ears back.
I crouch close against you.
We crouch at the burrow mouth.
I touch my nose to yours.
This burrow is deep enough for two.
I groom the fur on your back.
You hop ahead; I take the rear.
The meadow is quiet; perfect.
Do not run too far off.
We watch both directions.
I cup it with my forepaws.
Can this be bitten at all?
I carry it back to the burrow.
Too big; I cannot bite it.
I hide it under the grass.
I sniff at it for a good while.
I am taking this.
I push it about.
Shiny, but not food.
I bite it and spit it out.
I go rigid on the spot.
My ears go straight up.

lines.zh: 我背上的粗条纹，在草里最显眼。
lines.en: My bold stripes stand out in the grass.
My hind legs are tensed.
I fix on your direction.

lines.zh: 这不是兔子该待的地方
lines.en: This is no place for a rabbit.
I am ready to bolt at any moment.
The burrow is safer than out here.
One of my kind thumps the ground.
My nose stops twitching.
I track you with my eyes.
Move, and I change direction.
The burrow is only five hops away.
I press my body to the ground.
Do not close in from both sides.
My ears are reading your feet.
I edge backwards.
You stop; so do I.
I know this path well.
I will wait a bit longer.
I kick out at you with my hind legs.
I bite down hard once.
My forepaws rake down.
This is all the force I have.

lines.zh: 被逼到洞口的都会还手
lines.en: Even prey fights at its burrow.
I leap at your knee.
I strike once and retreat.
My stripes flare as a warning.

lines.zh: 粗条纹的兔子也会咬人。
lines.en: Even a striped rabbit bites back.
I am breathing very fast.
I poke my head from the burrow.
My bold stripes show first.
I raise my ears and listen round.
I hop onto the grass.
My nose starts twitching first.
I shake the dirt off my back.
The grass here grows well.
I dash a short distance.
I circle my own burrow.
I make one soft sound.
My fur smells singed.
My legs buckle on landing.
Water in my nose and I panic.
The blast flings me away.
Something pierces my hind leg.
That light leaves me dizzy.
Too hungry even to hop.
Lightning strikes; I lock up.
No grass under my feet.
